draft.title: Islamic environmental ethics
card: Muslims believe God created the earth and everything in it. The natural world belongs to God, not to humans.
a trustee or steward. The Quran describes humans as khalifa on earth, so they are entrusted with caring for creation and are answerable to God for how they treat it.
Because of this trust, many Muslims teach that wasting resources, polluting and harming animals are wrong. The Quran warns against wastefulness and corruption on the earth.
Many Muslims also link care for creation to hadith, which report the Prophet Muhammad urging kindness to animals and moderate use of water, even when washing for prayer.
draft.remember: People hold the earth in trust from God, so they are to care for it and not simply use it.

a.q: In Islamic environmental ethics, what does it mean to call humans khalifa?
opts: They are trustees who must care for God's creation
They are owners who may use the earth as they wish
They are rulers whose needs outrank all other creatures
They are guests who should leave nature untouched
a.why: Khalifa means trustee or steward. The earth belongs to God, so humans are responsible to God for how they treat it. Ownership is the tempting wrong answer, because the card says the world belongs to God, not to humans.
a.clue: Think about who the earth belongs to.

b.q: A Muslim council in Perth plans a community garden at its mosque. Which reason for it best reflects Islamic environmental ethics?
opts: Humans are trustees who answer to God for creation
Humans own the land so they may shape it as they like
Gardens raise the value of land held by the mosque
Nature has no value unless people can use it
b.why: The khalifa idea holds that people care for creation because they are trustees answerable to God. The ownership option is tempting, but it contradicts the belief that the earth belongs to God. The other options give reasons of profit or use, not trusteeship.
b.clue: Look for the reason that involves being answerable to God.

a.best: They are trustees who must care for God's creation

b.best: Humans are trustees who answer to God for creation

b.q: A Muslim council in Perth plans a community garden at its mosque. Which reason for it best reflects Islamic environmental ethics?
opts: Humans are trustees who answer to God for creation
God gave humans the land to shape as they like
God's creation exists only to serve human needs
Gardens raise the value of land held by the mosque
b.why: The khalifa idea holds that people care for creation because they are trustees answerable to God. The option that God gave humans the land to shape as they like is tempting, but it treats people as owners, and the card says the earth belongs to God. Saying creation exists only for human needs or for profit ignores the trust and the teaching against waste and harm.
b.clue: Ask whose land the garden is really on.
